comparisons.coverage_method: Verified the pinned manifest hash and all 135 local file hashes; reconciled all 130 BDDL definitions with the 130 tasks in the original five-suite libero_task_map, then searched the complete inventory for adjustment, locking, screw, nut, fastener, gripper, and articulated-control neighbors. Inspected the closest BDDL and its predicate backend.
comparisons.objective: Candidate sets a gripper opening stop to 90°, locks the setting, and verifies retained motion. LIBERO's closest rotational task only turns on a stove.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial driver and wrench seating, coupled screw/jam-nut countertorque, setting preservation, tool withdrawal, and repeated articulation. The LIBERO neighbor actuates one stove control through a unary TurnOn predicate.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a locked angle within tolerance, retained nuts, three repeatable cycles, bounded drift, and released clearance. LIBERO requires only the stove's Turnon predicate to become true.

closest_tasks.name: libero_90/KITCHEN_SCENE3_turn_on_the_stove
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Manipulate a stove control until its on-state is reached.
closest_tasks.success_condition: The goal is `(Turnon flat_stove_1)`; the predicate backend delegates to `arg.turn_on()`.
closest_tasks.reason: It shares rotary control actuation but has no adjustable stop, concentric screw and jam nut, counterholding, locked-setting preservation, or post-lock cycle verification.

comparisons.reason: The complete registered LIBERO task set contains rotary appliance actuation but no task testing coupled adjustment-and-locking under countertorque with retained cyclic function.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified the pinned manifest hash and all 381 local file hashes; covered 379 kitchen modules plus environments/__init__.py and the original dataset registry, including its atomic/composite task sets. Searched the complete class inventory for adjust, turn, lock, screw, fasten, tool, and articulated-control tasks and inspected the closest temperature-adjustment implementation.
comparisons.objective: Candidate calibrates and mechanically locks a robot-gripper opening stop, then verifies retention. RoboCasa's closest task changes a toaster-oven temperature setting.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate needs two-tool coaxial engagement and bimanual reaction-torque control. The RoboCasa neighbor turns a single appliance temperature control without a second locking element.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades final angular accuracy, jam-nut seating, retained hardware, repeated return angle, drift, and hands-off clearance. The RoboCasa neighbor succeeds after a temperature-state change of at least 0.15 in the requested direction.

closest_tasks.name: AdjustToasterOvenTemperature
closest_tasks.objective: Increase or decrease the toaster-oven temperature from its initial setting.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Rotate or otherwise manipulate one temperature control to change its scalar state.
closest_tasks.success_condition: Temperature must change by at least 0.15 in the selected direction.
closest_tasks.reason: Both change an adjustable setting, but RoboCasa does not lock the setting against jam-nut reaction or test retained articulated motion after tool release.

comparisons.reason: No registered RoboCasa task couples adjustment with a separate mechanical lock, required counterholding, and repeated functional retention.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified the pinned manifest hash and all 11 local file hashes; checked the original 25-entry ENVIRONMENTS/ENVIRONMENT_MAP registry against the two SimplerEnv root files and all nine selected ManiSkill2_real2sim environment modules. Searched every definition and inspected the closest articulated-joint task completely.
comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks the maximum opening of an angular gripper and verifies repeated retained opening. The closest SimplerEnv task opens a cabinet drawer.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate combines fine tool seating, countertorque, and later articulated cycling. The neighbor pulls one prismatic drawer joint past a threshold.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires locked 90° opening, low drift across three cycles, retained nuts, and released clearance. OpenDrawer succeeds when drawer qpos reaches 0.15 or more.

closest_tasks.name: google_robot_open_drawer / OpenDrawerCustomInScene-v0
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Grasp or contact a drawer and translate its prismatic joint.
closest_tasks.success_condition: The selected drawer joint position is at least 0.15.
closest_tasks.reason: It shares articulated motion only; it does not set a stop, manipulate fasteners with tools, preserve a setting under lock torque, or verify cycle-to-cycle retention.

comparisons.reason: The complete SimplerEnv registry consists of grasping, placement, relative movement, and drawer manipulation; none tests mechanical calibration and locking.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified the pinned manifest hash and all 1,122 local file hashes; covered all 1,119 BDDL activity definitions across both recorded corpus versions plus behavior_task.py, bddl_utils.py, and attached_to.py. Searched the complete activity inventory for assembly, attachment, screw, nut, lock, adjustment, and tool use, then inspected both closest BDDLs and the AttachedTo backend completely.
comparisons.objective: Candidate calibrates an angular-gripper stop, locks it without disturbing the setting, and verifies retained operation. The closest BEHAVIOR activities attach rigid components into a final assembly.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires real concentric driver/wrench engagement and countertorque. BEHAVIOR's AttachedTo state aligns male/female meta links and creates a fixed or spherical joint after proximity/orientation checks.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks numeric angle, nut retention, repeated cycles, drift, and released clearance. BEHAVIOR checks abstract `attached` relations between specified objects.

closest_tasks.name: attach_a_camera_to_a_tripod
closest_tasks.objective: Attach a digital camera to a tripod.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Bring compatible attachment meta links into positional and angular alignment; the backend then creates a joint.
closest_tasks.success_condition: The camera's AttachedTo state names the tripod as its parent.
closest_tasks.reason: A real camera may use a screw, but this corpus implementation exposes only meta-link alignment and automatic joint creation, not threaded adjustment, jam-nut counterholding, or retained-cycle verification.

closest_tasks.name: assembling_furniture
closest_tasks.objective: Attach a desk bracket to a top and all four legs to the bracket.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Align multiple compatible rigid attachment links to form an assembly.
closest_tasks.success_condition: The bracket-top and every leg-bracket `attached` relation must hold.
closest_tasks.reason: It is assembly-level attachment, but its resolved backend does not model fastener driving, two-tool reaction torque, an adjustable stop, or functional retention after cycling.

comparisons.reason: The plausible abstract attachment overlap is resolved by the backend: BEHAVIOR creates joints from aligned meta links rather than testing the candidate's coupled screw/jam-nut calibration mechanism.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified the pinned manifest hash and both complete local source files. Checked the manifest's authoritative ten-task catalog against all ten setup/instruction/reset/rubric records in official-setups.json and reviewed official-procedures.json; unselected thumbscrew and nut-bolt drafts were treated as industrial context, not benchmark tasks.
comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks an adjustable robot-gripper stop and proves retained repeated motion. The closest published DataCenterBench task turns a marked knob to a target.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires two separately seated tools, coupled screw/nut countertorque, and later lever cycling. DC-knob requires single-control rotary positioning.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires tight angular tolerances, seated and retained nuts, three consistent cycles, drift at most 2°, and released clearance. DC-knob scores the pointer's final relation to one goal mark.

closest_tasks.name: DC-knob — Turn the knob to the mark
closest_tasks.quote: Turn the round knob on the white box clockwise until the black line on it points at the black mark on the box.
closest_tasks.objective: Rotate a fixed dimmer knob clockwise to its marked goal.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Grasp or push one rotary control and regulate its final angle visually.
closest_tasks.success_condition: Full score when the knob line points at the goal mark; partial credit when it turns clockwise but stops short.
closest_tasks.reason: Both target an angular setting, but DC-knob has no independent locknut, reaction-sensitive setting preservation, tool use, or repeated post-lock function test.

comparisons.reason: None of the ten published DataCenterBench tasks tests locking an adjustable stop against countertorque and verifying retained cyclic function; draft fastener procedures are explicitly outside the task catalog.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified the pinned manifest hash and all 110 local file hashes. Reconciled 54 task modules with 54 same-named task configs; the sole extra config is the shared `_task.yml`, and task_registry.py dynamically resolves each same-named class. Searched the full config/module inventory and inspected Fasten Screws' config and implementation completely.
comparisons.objective: Candidate calibrates a gripper stop, secures it with a jam nut while preserving the setting, and validates repeated retained opening. RoboDojo Fasten Screws inserts and tightens three matched fasteners.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both involve coaxial fastener manipulation. Candidate additionally requires simultaneous driver counterholding and wrench rotation on a coupled screw/nut pair, followed by tool withdrawal and articulated verification; Fasten Screws checks nut/bolt alignment and insertion depth.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate's full score depends on angle accuracy, lock seating, retained hardware, three cycles, low drift, and clearance. Fasten Screws awards progress for one, two, or three nuts being upright, coaxially aligned within 1 mm, and inserted to the depth threshold, with grippers open.

closest_tasks.name: fasten_screws
closest_tasks.quote: Insert and tighten each screw into the nut of the same color.
closest_tasks.objective: Insert and tighten three screws into color-matched nuts.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Align separate fasteners coaxially and insert them to sufficient depth; the implementation does not require a wrench-held jam nut or preserved adjustable setting.
closest_tasks.success_condition: Each pair must have an upright nut, XY separation within 1 mm, and insertion depth meeting the 9 mm threshold; higher scores require more completed pairs and open grippers.
closest_tasks.reason: This is the closest suite neighbor because it tests fastener alignment and tightening, but it does not test locking a pre-adjusted screw against reaction torque or functional retention across cycles.

comparisons.reason: Fasten Screws shares a generic fastener primitive but measures insertion of independent screw/nut pairs, not the candidate's central coupled adjustment-preservation-and-retention ability.
